title: Integrability under fourth moment control
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $Z:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^4(\mu)$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously differentiable. If $C\ge 0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$, then $\omega\mapsto\psi(Z(\omega))$ is integrable under $\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: the absolute value of the fourth derivative of $\psi$ is bounded by $C$ everywhere
replaced: Let $Z\in L^4(\mu)$ be real-valued on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, and let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$. If some $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|$ for every real $t$, then $\psi(Z)$ is integrable under $\mu$.
